summary: Lookout site above Eagle Lake: a CCC-era two-story structure, then a 1975 solar-powered tower; NHLR-registered 1996; shutters replaced by Forest Service staff in 2020.

visit.trail_note: From Eagle Lake, turn left after the Summit Campsite (register visit report, June 2021).

events.note: Lookout station established to watch for fires (May 7, 1931 newspaper note)
Two-story structure built by the CCC, per the register
Alarm from the Antelope station; roughly 2,000-acre brush and grass fire on McDonald Peak
Lightning struck the station; lookout Ted Thompson temporarily blinded
Current tower; register gives 1975 as the build year
Solar-powered installation dedicated by the Forest Service (December 1978 item)
Old shutters replaced by Forest Service staff with a $500 FFLA restoration grant for materials

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the peak was first used as a lookout in the early 1900s and that a two-story CCC structure dated from 1933; the current tower is dated 1975. A 1931 newspaper note mentions a station already in use. The sources do not agree on when the lookout began.
The August 2020 register visit marked staffing as sometimes and the FFLA report says the lookout was unstaffed that season; the June 2021 register visit marked it staffed.

notes_for_editor: Access level and climbability are not stated by any source read, so the access and visit keys are left out. The FFLA California list at firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/ codes the lookout as a 2-Story Cab, Standing, NHLR US 182, CA 7, which matches the record's kind and the register. The record's $500 figure comes from cr-rest-2020.pdf, not the cr-ca-north-2020 report, which gives no amount. The 2021 staffed mark is five years old. A WebSearch turned up a trail-guide snippet saying the modern lookout is manned during fire season, but that page was not read, so it is not cited.
